newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola sees higher sales volumes.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola sees higher sales volumes.

text.p: Coca-Cola Co. said on Tuesday it expects worldwide unit case volume for its beverage business to increase seven to eight percent during the second quarter, led by rises of 10 to 11 percent in Latin America.
Worldwide gallon sales are expected to rise eight to nine percent, with sales in Latin America and Africa increasing 12 to 13 percent, the company said.
Oppenheimer & Co analyst Roy Burry said the volume numbers were not as strong as in the comparable period last year but fell within the expected range.
Prudential Securities analyst George Thompson said of the report, "It was equal to or in the upper end of the range that we were expecting."

Coca-Cola said North America unit case volume for Coca-Cola beverages was expected to be up 4 percent to 5 percent for the second quarter. Gallon sales of concentrate or syrup also were expected to rise 4 percent to 5 percent.

For Europe, unit case volume was seen rising 5 percent to 6 percent, while gallon sales were expected to rise 6 percent to 7 percent. In Africa, unit case volume was seen rising 6 percent to 7 percent. For the Middle and Far East, unit case volume was seen increasing 9 percent to 10 percent, with gallon sales also up 9 percent to 10 percent.
